problem: Perception and navigation models degrade under sensor corruption, viewpoint change, sensor-placement change and platform shift, and prior robustness benchmarks (e.g. RoboDrive) were vehicle-centric and covered a single domain.
motivation: Real deployments span cars, drones and legged robots, so robustness and cross-platform generalization must be evaluated systematically with shared data, baselines and protocols. The report consolidates a large community challenge to expose common design patterns and open problems.
key_idea: Organize a five-track challenge (driving VLM QA, social navigation, sensor-placement 3D detection, cross-modal drone retrieval, cross-platform 3D detection) with unified protocols, and distill trends from 23 winning solutions.
insight: Winning solutions gained more from training procedures (data-centric augmentation, pretraining, multi-sweep and placement-mixed training, pseudo-label filtering, prompt routing) than from architecture changes. Geometry-aware canonicalization and adaptation stability were recurring themes. Team ablations support this: Smartqiu's mAP rose 0.605→0.729→0.743 with multi-sweep aggregation and placement mixing alone; Visionary's ablation showed +2.99 from fine-tuning and +5.09 from viewpoint normalization on top of large-scale pretraining. Social navigation gains were small (Total 62.5→70.2), suggesting saturation.
method: Track 1 Driving with Language: DriveBench-based multi-view VLM QA under corruptions; MCQ accuracy and LLMScore; final = 0.2*Phase1 + 0.8*Phase2; baseline Qwen2.5-VL-7B
Track 2 Social Navigation: RGBD navigation in Social-HM3D (844 scenes, 0-6 humans), baseline Falcon; Total=0.4SR+0.3SPL+0.3PSC, ranked on Phase 2
Track 3 Sensor Placement: LiDAR 3D detection on Place3D CARLA data generalizing to unseen placements, baseline BEVFusion-L, nuScenes-style mAP/NDS
Track 4 Cross-Modal Drone Navigation: GeoText-190 text-to-aerial-image retrieval (33,516 queries, 11,172 images, 190 unseen categories), baseline X-VLM, score=(R@1+R@10)/2
Track 5 Cross-Platform 3D Detection: unsupervised adaptation from vehicle to drone (Phase 1) and quadruped (Phase 2) LiDAR, baseline PV-RCNN+ST3D++, 3D AP (R40)
Winning-solution synthesis: per-team method summaries (e.g. InternVL3-8B with pseudo-label pretraining, GBlobs, PE-MoE, DataEngine/LION) and cross-track discussion

setting.backbone: Varies by team (InternVL3-8B, Qwen2.5-VL-72B, BEVFusion-L, PV-RCNN++, LION, X-VLM etc.); challenge report, not a single model
setting.training_data: Challenge-provided datasets (DriveBench, Social-HM3D, Place3D, GeoText-1652/190, Pi3DET); teams add extra pseudo-labels or pretraining data (e.g. six LiDAR datasets)
setting.observation: Track-dependent: multi-view RGB with language (T1), egocentric RGB-D (T2), LiDAR (T3, T5), aerial images and text (T4)
setting.action_space: Social navigation track: low-level discrete agent actions in Habitat (Falcon); other tracks are not navigation
setting.simulator: Habitat (Social-HM3D) for Track 2; CARLA-based Place3D for Track 3

numbers.extra: Challenge hidden test, verified on EvalAI; success radius 0.2 m
numbers.evidence: Table 2 Track 2 Social Navigation results, Phase 2, Are Ivan row

numbers_note: This is a challenge report; only the social-navigation track (Track 2) is navigation-related and is listed. Other tracks (driving QA, 3D detection, retrieval) are not embodied navigation benchmarks so are omitted from numbers. Track 2 results are on the challenge's hidden Phase 2 test set, not an official canonical benchmark.
results: 143 teams from 85 institutions in 16 countries took part. Champions beat baselines substantially: Track 1 TQL final 61.00 vs Qwen2.5-VL-7B 43.5; Track 2 Are Ivan Total 70.2 vs Falcon 62.5 (SR 66.0 vs 54.0); Track 3 LRP mAP 0.784 vs BEVFusion-L 0.605; Track 4 lineng final 49.82 vs X-VLM 37.27; Track 5 mAP 58.54 vs PV-RCNN+ST3D++ 45.07.
limitations: Report summarizes leaderboards and team self-reports; there is no controlled comparison, and many ablation numbers come from team-supplied claims
Tasks are evaluated in isolation, so compound distribution shifts are not covered; the social navigation track is simulation-only with no real robot
Some reported details are inconsistent (e.g. Track 4 champion described on University-1652, differing team names between tables and text)
